name: Auto mode
summary: Let a safety check approve Claude's actions for you, so it can work through a task without constant prompts.
what: Auto mode is a permission mode. Instead of asking you about each action, Claude Code sends it to a separate classifier model first. Reading files and editing inside your project go ahead; actions that go beyond what you asked for, touch unfamiliar systems or seem driven by untrusted content are blocked. Your own deny and ask rules still apply on top.

impact.title: Longer tasks without babysitting
impact.detail: Claude keeps going through routine steps instead of stopping for approval at each one.

impact.title: Guardrails stay on
impact.detail: Risky actions are blocked, and after several blocks in a row Claude Code goes back to asking you.

impact.title: Your rules still win
impact.detail: Deny rules block in every mode, and ask rules still force a prompt.

howItWorks: Press Shift+Tab until the status bar shows auto mode, or start with claude --permission-mode auto.
To start in it every time, set permissions.defaultMode to auto in ~/.claude/settings.json (project files can't set it).
Read-only actions and edits in the working folder are approved; other actions are checked by the classifier first.
Blocked actions don't run, and you can review them later under /permissions.
It needs a recent model, and admins can turn it off with permissions.disableAutoMode.

events.note: First changelog mention of auto mode; it shipped earlier without an entry.
Denied actions show a notification and can be retried from /permissions.
